s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of severe upper abdominal pain with associated nausea and vomiting, worsened by oral intake, in a post-surgical patient
salient_findings: Sudden-onset, sharp upper abdominal pain rated 9/10
Pain worsened with oral intake
Associated nausea and vomiting
Generalized abdominal tenderness, most pronounced in the right hypochondrium
Abnormal contrast-enhanced abdominal CT findings with a cluster of small-bowel loops and spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels
key_facts: Pain awakened her early in the morning
Unable to tolerate liquids or a soft diet
History of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass three weeks prior
History of laparoscopic cholecystectomy and other abdominal surgeries
Generalized abdominal tenderness, most pronounced in the right hypochondrium
Laboratory studies showed normal liver function tests and hemoglobin
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a cluster of small-bowel loops and spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels

shortlist.label: Internal hernia
shortlist.why_kept: History of recent abdominal surgery and CT findings of small-bowel loops and spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels

shortlist.label: Intestinal obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden-onset severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake

shortlist.label: Adhesive bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: History of multiple abdominal surgeries and presentation of bowel obstruction symptoms

shortlist.label: Mesenteric ischemia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to physical findings and CT findings of mesenteric vessel congestion

shortlist.label: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complication
shortlist.why_kept: Recent history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and presentation of severe abdominal pain and nausea

raw.rationale: The contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a cluster of small-bowel loops and a spiral pattern of central mesenteric vessels, which is consistent with internal hernia, especially given the patient's recent history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass

rejected.label: Intestinal obstruction
rejected.why: There were no signs of anastomotic leak, strangulation, or bowel obstruction on the CT scan

rejected.label: Adhesive bowel obstruction
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and CT findings are more consistent with internal hernia than adhesive bowel obstruction

rejected.label: Mesenteric ischemia
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory studies showed normal lactate and no signs of bowel ischemia

rejected.label: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complication
rejected.why: While the patient's recent surgery is a risk factor, the specific findings on CT are more consistent with internal hernia than a general complication of the surgery
